title: Aerolíneas Argentinas Flight 386 en route from Lima, Peru to Los Angeles, USA, experiences a severe health crisis. Passengers consume in-flight meals contaminated with cholera, leading to 75 reported cases of illness and a fatality.
text: On 14 February 1992, food contaminated with cholera was distributed to the passengers on Aerolíneas Argentinas Flight 386, operated by a Boeing 747-200. One of the passengers died from the illness.

title: A suicide bomber attacks the Israeli embassy in Buenos Aires. 29 civilians are killed in the attack and 242 additional civilians are injured. The Islamic Jihad Organization claim responsibility.
text: The attack on the Israeli embassy in Buenos Aires was a suicide bombing attack on the building of the Israeli embassy of Argentina, located in Buenos Aires, which was carried out on 17 March 1992. 29 civilians were killed in the attack and 242 additional civilians were injured.

title: A powerful F4 tornado strikes the small village of Estación López in Buenos Aires Province. Ninety percent of the village's structures are destroyed, as vehicles are tossed hundreds of meters, along with four fatalities. It stands as one…

title: Argentina defeats host nation Saudi Arabia 3-1 to win the King Fahd Cup.
text: The Argentina national football team, nicknamed la Albiceleste, represents Argentina in men's international football and is administered by the Argentine Football Association, the governing body of football in Argentina. It has been a member of FIFA since 1912 and was a founding member of CONMEBOL in 1916.

title: A dentist named Ricardo Barreda murders his wife, two daughters, and mother-in-law.
text: Ricardo Alberto Barreda was an Argentine dentist who was sentenced to life imprisonment for the murders of his wife, Gladys McDonald, his two daughters, Cecilia and Adriana Barreda, and his mother-in-law, Elena Arreche, on 15 November 1992. He was granted parole on 29 March 2011.

title: Argentina at the 1992 Summer Paralympics
text: Argentina competed at the 1992 Summer Paralympics in Barcelona, Spain. 27 competitors from Argentina won 2 medals, 1 gold and 1 silver, to finish 40th in the medal table.

title: Argentina at the 1992 Summer Olympics
text: Argentina competed at the 1992 Summer Olympics in Barcelona, Spain. 84 competitors, 67 men and 17 women, took part in 68 events in 17 sports.

title: 1992 Argentina rugby union tour of Europe
text: The 1992 Argentina rugby union tour of Europe was a series of eight matches played by the Argentina national rugby union team in October and November 1992, in France, Spain and Romania. The renewed and young Argentinian team won all the test match.
wiki: 1992 Argentina rugby union tour of Europe

title: 1992 Campeonato Argentino de Rugby
text: The 1992 Campeonato Argentino de Rugby was won by the Tucumàn who gained their title after the defeat of Córdoba. The 19 teams were divided in the championship; "Campeonato", "Ascenso", "Classificacion".

title: 1992 France rugby union tour of Argentina
text: The 1992 France rugby union tour of Argentina was a series of match played by France rugby union team in June and July 1992, in Argentina. France won both the official test match against the Pumas.
wiki: 1992 France rugby union tour of Argentina

title: Argentina at the 1992 Winter Olympics
text: Argentina competed at the 1992 Winter Olympics in Albertville, France.

title: Asteroid 5751 Zao is discovered by Masahiro Koishikawa.
text: An asteroid is a minor planet that orbits within the inner Solar System or is co-orbital with a planet. These objects are larger than a meteoroid (thus 1 meter or larger) and are neither a planet nor an identified comet.

title: First confirmed detection of exoplanets with announcement of the discovery of several terrestrial-mass planets orbiting the pulsar PSR B1257+12 by radio astronomers Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail working in the United States.
text: An exoplanet or extrasolar planet is a planet outside the Solar System. The first confirmed detection of an exoplanet was in 1992 around a pulsar, and the first detection around a main-sequence star was in 1995.

title: Discovery of 15760 Albion, the first trans-Neptunian object to be found after Pluto and Charon.
text: 15760 Albion is the first trans-Neptunian object discovered after Pluto and Charon. Measuring about 108–167 kilometres in diameter, it was discovered in 1992 by David C. Jewitt and Jane X. Luu at the Mauna Kea Observatory, Hawaii.

title: Pope John Paul II issues an apology and lifts the 1633 edict of the Inquisition against Galileo Galilei.
text: Pope John Paul II was the head of the Catholic Church and sovereign of Vatican City from 16 October 1978 until his death in 2005. He was the first non-Italian pope since Adrian VI in the 16th century, as well as the third longest-serving pope in history, after St.

title: The Goosebumps series of children's horror fiction, penned by R. L. Stine, is first published in the United States.
text: Robert Lawrence Stine is an American novelist. He is the writer of Goosebumps, a horror fiction novel series for children which has sold over 400 million copies globally in 35 languages, becoming the second-best-selling book series in history.

title: An attempt is made to set fire to the National Library of Abkhazia in Sukhumi during the War in Abkhazia by Georgian forces.
text: The War in Abkhazia was fought between Georgian government and paramilitary forces, and a coalition of Abkhaz separatist forces and North Caucasian militants between 1992 and 1993. Ethnic Georgians who lived in Abkhazia fought largely on the side of Georgian government forces.

title: The National and University Library of Bosnia and Herzegovina is annihilated during the Siege of Sarajevo by the Army of Republika Srpska.
text: The Siege of Sarajevo was a prolonged military blockade of Sarajevo, the capital of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, during the Bosnian War. Beginning on 5 April 1992, the capital was surrounded by Bosnian Serb forces following the outbreak of the Bosnian War.

title: Michael Ondaatje's historiographic metafiction The English Patient is published in Canada. It will win The Golden Man Booker in 2018.
text: Philip Michael Ondaatje is a Sri Lankan-born Canadian poet, fiction writer and essayist. Ondaatje's literary career began with his poetry: in 1967 he published The Dainty Monsters, and in 1970 the critically acclaimed The Collected Works of Billy the Kid.

title: British fashion designer Alexander McQueen shows his first collection, partly inspired by The Silence of the Lambs (film).
text: Lee Alexander McQueen was a British fashion designer and couturier. Known for his unconventional designs, he was one of the most influential fashion designers in the world from the early 1990s until his death by suicide in 2010.

title: Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum in Madrid is opened to the public as a gallery for the private art collection of the Thyssen-Bornemisza family.
text: The Thyssen-Bornemisza National Museum, or simply the Thyssen, is an art museum in Madrid, Spain, located near the Prado Museum on one of the city's main boulevards. It is known as part of the "Golden Triangle of Art", which also includes the Prado and the Reina Sofía national galleries.
